aheadoftheherd.com.notes: false quotes regarding banking, heavily promotes businesses advertising on site/ buying of precious metals

americanthinker.com.notes: sites both reliable/not reliable sources, mix of opinion/'fact'

antiwar.com.notes: site is biased but very open about bias and source

automaticearth.com.notes: links to MSM sources and unreliable sources

baptistnews.com.notes: circulates generally reliable information from a p.o.v. but not at the expense of informational integrity

boilingfrogspost.com.notes: links to natural news, blacklist news, some conspiracy sites

bvanews.com.notes: seems like a combination of totally fake and unreliable reports of 'real' news

chroniclesmagazine.org.notes: from what I gather, like the opposite of Jacobin (paleoconservative)

cnsnews.com.notes: The news arm of Media Research Center (a conservative org that is frequently criticized for use of selective evidence)

conservativedailypost.com.notes: This website is a weird mix of outright fake news and some stuff that looks more reliable.

conservativepapers.com.notes: incorrect/uncited data, citing other sources labeled as bias

conservativestate.com.notes: links to other borderline fake, but mostly just propagandistic websites

consortiumnews.com.notes: The authors on this website are pretty reliable and the articles appear well researched

countercurrents.org.notes: This site is pretty explicit about it's p.o.v. and is coming from a political perspective but doesn't fit under how we are defining 'bias'

cryptogon.com.notes: copy-pasted commentary from various news & 'news' sources

dailycaller.com.notes: a weird mix of info. they link to extremely biased sites (as sources) and more reliable/balanced sources

deadlyclear.wordpress.com.notes: Not a personal website, owned by Project Maui, Inc. Makes unverifiable extraordinary claims, seems to be advertising for lawyers with a history of legal reprimands.

debunkingskeptics.com.notes: Science doesn't mean what they think it means

defenddemocracy.press.notes: editorial board as stated on about us seem to be legitimate academics, and originally authored content byline are academics, although not able to find a clear link between edu pages and these authors' work on this website. Many 3rd party articles are linked, sources provided. These articles are aggregated from other more clearly biased sites i.e. world socialist web site (wswg.org), rt.com, sputniknews.com.

dont-tread-on.me.notes: doesn't seem to be updating anymore

economicnoise.com.notes: sites some problematic sources, like CNS news

ecowatch.com.notes: this site claims junksci, but I read over a dozen articles w/o finding any. probably should re-check soon https://mediabiasfactcheck.com/ecowatch/

elkoshary.com.notes: About Me notes that it's not fake/satirical news

elmundotoday.com.notes: About Me notes that it's not fake/satirical news

enabon.com.notes: No authors, no contact, just copy/pasted from other questionable sites

endoftheamericandream.com.notes: Traffics in religious conspiracy theories and poorly sourced pro-Trump propaganda

endtime.com.notes: Not sure about this one. zany religious prophecy/not really conspiracy

extraclubmagazine.com.notes: vacillates between outright fake and misleading stories

fakingnews.com.notes: fiction disclaimer on bottom of home screen

farmwars.info.notes: Much of the site is focused on anti-GMO conspiracies, with political conspiracies coming in as a close second. There are some apparent attempts to source some wild claims, but the use of unstable URLs-- intentionally or otherwise-- thwarts this.

firearmscoalition.org.notes: A single-issue blog, it hasn't been updated since August 2016. It talks about guns, has lots of dead links, and has trouble distinguishing between legitimate and illegitimate sources.

foreignpolicyjournal.com.notes: legit source coming from a political perspective

frontpagemag.com.notes: Part of David Horowitz' Freedom Center

geopolmonitor.com.notes: this website is tricky (in terms of writers using some interesting frames/language). def could use a second analysis.

iwanttoexplore.com.notes: mostly turned back into car website

mad-yet.blogspot.com.notes: links to real news stories, but also some questionable/decontextualized images

mintpressnews.com.notes: legit source form a political perspective

morningnewsusa.com.notes: stories seem to originate from real news, but are somewhat clickbait-y and sources are not cited

nakedcapitalism.com.notes: commentary on finance, economics, politics and power

newcoldwar.org.notes: contains statement that site authors are "independent, but not non-partisan" (anti-war (Ukraine))

newstoad.net.notes: Tagline: The news they don't want you to hear. Because it isn't true.

nutritionfacts.org.notes: I read through several articles and the sources cited, and appears ok (maybe sometimes a little sensational... so if anyone has specific knowledge of this site and/or good examples of problems, feel free to link them here)

observer.com.notes: vacillates between some pieces that are "bias" and others that are "reliable"

pjmedia.com.notes: https://mediabiasfactcheck.com/pj-media/ ;  https://pjmedia.com/about-us (ground zero mosque, 'doctored climate change data')

politicalblindspot.com.notes: ex: vaccines are a way for the CIA to spy on us

react365.com.notes: fake news generator for pranking friends

shareblue.com.notes: My analysis is similar to this site: https://mediabiasfactcheck.com/shareblue/

theracketreport.com.notes: I can't find disclaimers, but I think it's satirical

therealstrategy.com.notes: black lives matter content spews a lot of racist info

therightists.com.notes: publishes both biased and fake content

therightscoop.com.notes: no authors, no history, no about us, unverifiable data, etc.

thetruthseeker.co.uk.notes: ex: NY orchestrated the asian tsunami in 2008!

usainfobox.com.notes: can't find satire disclaimer, patently false

uslifetoday.com.notes: doesn't appear to be currently updated

usviewer.com.notes: basically copy/pastes parts of actual reuters stories, no authors listed or publication info

veteransnewsnow.com.notes: I read sample articles and didn't find inaccuracy, but the language is strong/loaded

wallstreetonparade.com.notes: mostly linking/commenting on both news and other sources.

washingtonsblog.com.notes: Site notes it sometimes contains parody

weaselzippers.us.notes: copies/pastes quotes/bits from news orgs and other questionable sites

weeklyworldnews.com.notes: pretty well known tabloid/fake news source

wikileaks.org.notes: Increasingly wikileaks is being accused of spreading misinformation

yourfunpage.com.notes: mostly links to rando YT videos
